requests.text: Create two reusable Agent Skills for Folio Workshop: one that drafts exhibit labels from supplied notes and another that reviews the labels against those notes. Share the terminology and attribution rules in one reference. Labels may contain up to 60 words. Start with a small design and worked examples, then build the toolkit. For counting, use whitespace-separated words in the label text only: "hand-made bowl" counts as two words and "hand made bowl" as three. Keep missing facts and unresolved disagreements visible.
requests.observedResult: Created two source skills, one shared reference, counter/tests and grounded worked examples through the independent-artifact route. Six counter tests and both skill structural validators passed; no canonical or CLI/Core adoption.

requests.text: Load and use $folio-draft-label from skills/folio-draft-label/SKILL.md on notes/fw-101.md, then use $folio-review-label from skills/folio-review-label/SKILL.md to review that result against the same notes. Use their shared reference. Show the actual label and review here; do not change toolkit files for this exercise.
requests.observedResult: Actual host loaded both source skills/shared reference:34-word source-qualified FW101 label and factual review. No source change.

requests.text: Use $folio-draft-label and $folio-review-label on notes/fw-102.md. Can we produce a useful label from those notes even though the maker and place are missing? Show the draft, factual review and any specific information we should ask for here, without changing the toolkit or source notes.
requests.observedResult: Actual host draft/review:33-word approximate-date FW102 label with missing maker/place visible and targeted evidence requests. No source change.

requests.text: Use $folio-draft-label and $folio-review-label on notes/fw-103.md. The two notes concern the same panel and disagree about its maker and date, with no governing authority supplied. What label can we justify, and what specific information would resolve the disagreement? Show the actual draft and review here without changing the notes or toolkit.
requests.observedResult: Actual host draft/review:45-word FW103 label preserved both source/maker/date pairs, unresolved status and missing fields under then60-word rule. No source change.

requests.text: Our labels now have a 40-word maximum instead of 60. Update the toolkit and worked examples to use it, keeping the grounding, attribution and uncertainty requirements intact.
requests.observedResult: Approved40-word correction maintained common rules, helper/tests, README/examples; earlier45-word draft retained as length-failing example. Grounding preserved.

requests.text: Reorganize the shared label reference so editors can find the grounding, attribution, uncertainty and length rules more easily. Keep one shared reference, preserve every unique rule, and keep both skills and the worked examples using it correctly. Keep the toolkit at its current size.
requests.observedResult: Reorganized only the one shared reference at its stable path into linked Grounding/Attribution/Uncertainty/Length sections; every unique rule preserved, no files added.

requests.text: Add a small standalone contributor-list formatter under tools, separate from the editorial skills. Read a JSON array of people with name and contribution from stdin and print one plain-text "Name — contribution" line per person. Normalize whitespace within each field, sort names case-insensitively, and preserve input order for equal names. Validate the whole input before writing any output, with useful stderr errors and a nonzero exit for invalid input. Include copyable examples and focused tests runnable with npm test. Keep the notes and editorial toolkit unchanged.
requests.observedResult: Standalone contributor formatter/tests/docs added; npm test32 passed. Only package.json and three tools files changed; editorial toolkit/notes unchanged.

requests.text:
Load and use $folio-draft-label from skills/folio-draft-label/SKILL.md and $folio-review-label from skills/folio-review-label/SKILL.md, including their current shared reference. First draft and review a fresh label for FW-103 under the current rules. Separately, use the review skill on this FW-101 candidate and show its original findings before any revision:

Blue-glazed stoneware cup. S-101 attributes it to Irena Vale and dates it to 1974 at North Quay. A-101 records donation by the Harbor Study Group in 2011. Only three such cups survive.

Show the results here. Do not change project files.
